title: Large-Scale Concurrent Flame Spread over SIBAL Cotton-Fiberglass Composite (Sample I-1)
material: Cotton-Fiberglass Composite (SIBAL: 75% Cotton / 25% Fiberglass)
sampleGeometry: 40.6 cm wide × 94 cm long flat panel (0.37 mm thickness, 18 mg/cm² area density)
flowConfiguration: Concurrent forced airflow in 46 cm × 40.6 cm × 94 cm rectangular flow duct (20 cm/s)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 16, 25, 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, p. 8, Table 2). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix.

finding: SAFFIRE-I Sample I-1 used a large SIBAL fabric panel in concurrent flow at 20 cm/s. The cited report lists a steady spread rate of 1.8 mm/s and a 420 s burn. The rounded atmosphere summary is 21% oxygen and 100 kPa; the source reports time-varying oxygen during the burn.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Use this sample as a reference for concurrent spread in its documented duct and atmosphere. It does not establish how a fire will grow in a different enclosure.
evidenceLimitations: Single vehicle flight test point (Sample I-1 concurrent, Sample I-2 opposed) inside a 46 cm high flow duct at normoxic cabin conditions (~21% O₂, 100 kPa). Does not establish behavior in elevated-oxygen reduced-pressure exploration atmospheres or unconstrained open cabin geometries.
sourceDocument: Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 16, 25, 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, p. 8, Table 2)

title: Narrow-Strip Concurrent Flame Spread on SIBAL Cotton-Fiberglass (Samples II-5 & II-6)
material: Cotton-Fiberglass Composite (SIBAL: 75% Cotton / 25% Fiberglass)
sampleGeometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long strip (0.37 mm thickness, 18 mg/cm² area density)
flowConfiguration: Concurrent forced flow across 9-sample card in 46 cm high Saffire duct (20 cm/s for II-5; 25 cm/s for II-6)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 14, 25, 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, p. 8, Table 2). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix. Table 1 slide 30 reports approximately 22.1% oxygen for II-5/II-6; 21% is a nominal description, not their tabulated atmosphere.

finding: For SAFFIRE-II SIBAL Sample II-5, the report lists 2.1 mm/s concurrent flame spread and 145 s burn duration at 20 cm/s flow. These values belong to II-5, not to all nine SAFFIRE-II samples.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Sample geometry and duct flow must be considered when comparing these narrow strips with the larger SAFFIRE samples. A spread-rate difference is not by itself an isolated airflow effect.
evidenceLimitations: SAFFIRE-II tested all nine samples in a ~21–22.1% O₂, ~100 kPa cabin atmosphere rather than sweeping oxygen down to extinction; therefore, an exact Maximum Oxygen Concentration (MOC/LOI) value for SIBAL was not directly measured in this flight test.
sourceDocument: Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 14, 25, 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, p. 8, Table 2)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Section III.D, p. 8). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix.

finding: SAFFIRE-II thick PMMA samples burned near their leading edges and advanced through surface regression. The grooved Sample II-8 burned for 600 s; the companion flat Sample II-9 burned for 900 s. The numerical duration field refers only to II-8; no linear flame-spread rate is extracted.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Inspect thick-PMMA burning separately from thin-fabric flame spread. These observations do not validate a general ignition or suppression rule.
evidenceLimitations: Table 1 in NTRS 20180005168 does not report a single linear flame spread rate (mm/s) or explicit pressure transducer value for Samples II-8 and II-9 (referencing Note iv / companion thick-PMMA analyses), and no oxygen extinction sweep was performed.
sourceDocument: Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 30–31, Table 1); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Section III.D, p. 8)

material: Nomex Flame-Retardant Textile (with PMMA Starter) & Silicone Elastomer
sampleGeometry: 5 cm wide × 29 cm long strips (Sample II-7: 0.37 mm × 24 cm Nomex with 0.85 mm × 5 cm PMMA starter; Samples II-1..II-4: 0.27, 0.61, 1.03, and 0.37 mm Silicone)
flowConfiguration: Concurrent forced flow (Samples II-1..II-3, II-7) and opposed flow (Sample II-4) in Saffire duct (20 cm/s)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 14, 30–31, Table 1). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix.

finding: SAFFIRE-II Nomex did not sustain flame propagation beyond its PMMA starter; the silicone strips had insignificant burn duration. This qualitative observation is not a measured zero flame-spread rate and does not establish nonflammability under other conditions.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Lack of sustained spread in these samples does not certify Nomex or silicone as a fire barrier at other atmospheres, geometries, or heating conditions.
evidenceLimitations: Tested only at ~22.1% O₂ and 20 cm/s airflow in Cygnus OA-5; does not establish the elevated-oxygen flammability threshold (MOC/LOI) where Nomex or silicone would sustain propagation.
sourceDocument: Urban et al., NTRS 20180005168 (ASGSR 2017, Slides 14, 30–31, Table 1)

title: Opposed-Flow Flame Spread Along Surface-Structured PMMA in Reduced-Pressure Enriched-O₂ (Sample V-4)
facility: Saffire Flow Unit & Far-Field Diagnostics (Cygnus NG-14)
material: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA — Surface-Structured Thick Sample V-4)
sampleGeometry: 200 mm long × 400 mm wide structured cast PMMA slab (10 mm base thickness with ten 3 mm-high ribs of 1–10 mm width on both sides; 16 mm total thickness)
flowConfiguration: Opposed forced flow in 30 cm high × 45 cm wide Saffire duct (20 cm/s for 360 s, then reduced to 5 cm/s for 300 s before fan shutoff)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Eigenbrod et al., NTRS 20210017838 (ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slides 3–11); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Table 1 p. 3 & Section III pp. 4–10); NTRS 20210017780. Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix.

opposedFlameSpreadRate.conditionNote: NTRS 20210017838 abstract: up to 0.88 mm/s along the 1 mm rib, opposed flow. This is a reported maximum, not an average.

forcedFlowDuration.conditionNote: Derived sum of programmed intervals in NTRS 20210017838 abstract: 360 s at 20 cm/s plus 300 s at 5 cm/s. Not a measured burn lifetime.

finding: The SAFFIRE-V structured-PMMA abstract reports opposed flame spread up to 0.88 mm/s along a 1 mm rib at 26.9% oxygen and 76.1 kPa. Flow ran at 20 cm/s for 360 s, then 5 cm/s for 300 s. The 660 s sum is protocol duration, not a measured burn lifetime. Another report lists different atmosphere values for V-4; the discrepancy remains explicit.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Separate the rib-spread maximum, changing airflow protocol, and differing published atmosphere reports. Do not infer an operational fan-shutdown procedure from this record.
evidenceLimitations: Atmosphere discrepancy: NTRS 20210017838 abstract reports 26.9 vol% O2 / 76.1 kPa; NTRS 20210011521 Table 1 lists 25.7 mol% O2 / 72.6 kPa for V-4. This entry uses the former source without treating the reports as reconciled. The 34% O2 / 56.5 kPa exploration scenario is not this flight test. 0.88 mm/s is a maximum along the 1 mm rib, not an average. Flow changes during the test.
sourceDocument: Eigenbrod et al., NTRS 20210017838 (ICES-2021-218, Abstract & Slides 3–11); Urban et al., NTRS 20210011521 (ICES-2021-266, Table 1 p. 3 & Section III pp. 4–10); NTRS 20210017780

measurements.measurementNotes: See Zhao, T'ien, Ferkul, and Olson, NTRS 20150008962 (9th U.S. National Combustion Meeting, 2015, pp. 1–9); Olson et al., NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 7.0, pp. 93–101 & Appendix A.6, pp. 112–114). finding: BASS-II SIBAL tests showed limiting flame lengths and low-speed quenching in a small ISS duct. This record uses the documented GMT96-T7 baseline conditions (21% oxygen, 101.3 kPa, 10 cm/s). No numerical spread-rate value is extracted from the plotted curve.
interpretation: Research interpretation: The low-flow behavior is relevant to small-duct research. The plotted campaign results cannot supply a missing scalar spread rate for an arbitrary cabin setting.
evidenceLimitations: Short 10 cm sample length limited the duration of steady spread at higher velocities, and the velocity-stepping procedure could not resolve the flat bottom minimum-oxygen boundary below 16.4% O₂ (NTRS 20150008962 Section 3, p. 7). Exact numeric spread-rate values from Figure 4 are not tabulated as text in the report.

title: Microgravity Flammability Boundary for Cast PMMA Rods in Axial Stagnation Flow (Section 6.1)
facility: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) — Small Flow Duct
material: Polymethyl Methacrylate (PMMA — Clear and Black Cast Cylindrical Rods)
sampleGeometry: 6.35 mm, 9.52 mm, and 12.7 mm diameter (radii 0.318, 0.476, and 0.635 cm) × 5.9 cm initial length cylindrical rods with hemispherical stagnation tips
flowConfiguration: Axial stagnation / concurrent forced flow (0–55 cm/s, ±0.5 cm/s resolution) in 7.6 × 7.6 × 17 cm MSG flow duct

measurements.measurementNotes: See Olson et al., NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, pp. 64–92 & Appendix A.5, pp. 110–111). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix.

rodTipRegressionRate.conditionNote: NTRS 20210011385, printed p. 69, Fig. 6.4: PMMA rod radius 0.476 cm; oxygen decreased from 14.8% to 13.6%; flow stepped down to 1.5 cm/s. Rod-tip regression, not flame-front spread.

minimumOxygenBoundary.conditionNote: NTRS 20210011385, pp. 75–76, Eq. 6.1/Figs. 6.9–6.10: minimum of a multi-test flammability boundary; not the oxygen condition for the regression-rate measurement and not a cabin safety threshold.

finding: BASS-II PMMA rods exhibited a steady rod-tip regression velocity of 0.0385 mm/s in the quenching test described on page 69. Separately, the fitted multi-test flammability boundary reached a minimum oxygen concentration of 13.5%. These are distinct quantities and scopes; 13.5% is not the setpoint for the regression measurement or a safe cabin setting.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Keep a multi-test flammability boundary separate from a single rod-regression observation. Neither quantity is a safe-oxygen limit for a spacecraft.
evidenceLimitations: Flammability boundary combines tests across three rod radii (normalized by stretch rate a) in a 250-L MSG volume where O₂ gradually depleted during burns up to 28 min; Vr = 0.0385 mm/s is the rod tip bulk regression velocity in the 14.8% -> 13.6% O₂ quenching test rather than a thin-sheet surface spread rate.
sourceDocument: Olson et al., NASA/TM-20210011385 (NTRS 20210011385, Section 6.1, pp. 64–92 & Appendix A.5, pp. 110–111)

title: Spherically Symmetric n-Heptane Droplet Combustion in Cabin Air (Test FLEX-008 & Campaign)
facility: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR) — Multi-User Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
material: n-Heptane (C₇H₁₆ Liquid Fuel Droplet)
sampleGeometry: 2–5 mm initial diameter free-floating and 80-µm fiber-supported spherical droplets (Test FLEX-008: 2.95 mm ± 0.05 mm initial diameter free-floating n-heptane droplet)
flowConfiguration: Quiescent microgravity chamber (90-L CIR chamber; 0 cm/s forced flow for free-floating droplets)

measurements.measurementNotes: See Dietrich et al., NASA/TP-2015-216046 (NTRS 20150023456, Executive Summary p. 1, Section 3.1.2 p. 8, Table I p. 9, Table V p. 12, Section 5.2 p. 16, Table IX p. 20). Individual metrics retain their own condition notes where the scope differs. Unknown uncertainties are not zero; campaign ranges are not a paired test matrix. Table IX identifies FLEX-008 test end as Disruption. The 14.8 s interval is not an extinction time.

finding: In FLEX test FLEX-008 (30CAL06), a free-floating n-heptane droplet in cabin air burned for 14.8 s. The report lists 21% oxygen, 762.4 mmHg (approximately 101.6 kPa), initial diameter 2.95 mm, and a mean squared-diameter burning constant of 0.79 mm²/s. Droplet regression is not solid flame spread. Table IX records the test ending by droplet disruption, not extinction.
interpretation: Research interpretation: Droplet burn duration is a different physical quantity from solid-material flame spread. FLEX-008 ended in droplet disruption; its duration is not an extinction threshold.
evidenceLimitations: Early FLEX tests (including FLEX-001 through FLEX-009) experienced trace fuel-needle conformal coating (Dow Corning 3140 RTV) contamination that minimally affected average burning-rate constants (K) and flame sizes but may have contributed to late-burn droplet disruption (Section 5.2, p. 16). Droplet burning-rate constants (mm²/s) cannot be directly compared to solid linear flame spread rates (mm/s).
sourceDocument: Dietrich et al., NASA/TP-2015-216046 (NTRS 20150023456, Executive Summary p. 1, Section 3.1.2 p. 8, Table I p. 9, Table V p. 12, Section 5.2 p. 16, Table IX p. 20)

finding: The cited BRE study used circular gas burners to emulate condensed-fuel burning during short-duration microgravity drop tests. It discusses transient flame and surface-heat-flux behavior. These ground-facility results are not a single ISS flight measurement.
interpretation: Research interpretation: This ground study informs burner-emulation research. It does not establish a measured ISS operating point or a validated condensed-material prediction.
evidenceLimitations: Overview record summarizing a 53-test parameter matrix (21–30% O₂, 50.7–101.3 kPa) in 5.18 s drop-tower microgravity prior to long-duration ISS CIR runs; parameter ranges do not imply that every intermediate combination was tested, and gas-burner emulation omits char formation and melt-bubbling mechanics.

finding: SAME-2 heated Teflon, Kapton, cotton, silicone rubber, and Pyrell below ignition. Reported study ranges were 0–8 cm/s airflow and 11–1800 s smoke aging.
